Comments: No evidence found of farmer registries or agricultural systems integrated with a data exchange platform. Agriculture is not specifically addressed in Ghana's data exchange documentation.

revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) rested only on the general DIAL Ghana case study PDF, which does not specifically discuss agriculture. Searches on Ghana's agricultural digitisation found the Commonwealth Secretariat's 2024 National Agricultural Data Infrastructure policy brief, the existing Ag Data Hub/GhAAP platforms, and a February 2026 MoU for a new 'Akuafoɔ Anidasoɔ' farmer registration and subsidy platform (pilot from March 2026) — all fragmented systems with no link to a cross-government exchange. revised_comments: Ghana has several distinct agricultural digitisation initiatives — including the Ag Data Hub Ghana, the Ghana Agriculture and Agribusiness Platform (GhAAP) farmer registration module, and the newly announced 'Akuafoɔ Anidasoɔ' national farmer registration and subsidy platform (MoU signed February 2026, pilot from March 2026) — but none of these are integrated with a cross-government data exchange. Ghana's national data exchange itself remains at the legislative proposal stage, with the NITA Data Harmonisation Bill 2025 only opened for public consultation in November 2025 and not yet enacted. Agricultural data therefore remains siloed from other government systems.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: No documented operational integration between education systems and a national data exchange. Integration of the Ghana Card with education services (school enrollment, credentials) is noted as a future aspiration but no specific operational linkages documented. Ghana Card issuance at birth to all health facilities for school registration is recommended but not yet operational.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) cited a DPI Africa article on Ghana Card limitations that is not specific to education. Found a September 2025 announcement by the National Identification Authority of concrete plans to integrate the student database with the Ghana Card, alongside the existing GESMIS staff/learner portal (launched December 2024). Score changed from 0 to 2 (Planned) reflecting this specific, named but not-yet-implemented integration initiative rather than a genuine unknown.
revised_comments: Ghana's education sector has established management information systems — including the Education Management Information System (EMIS) and the Ghana Education Service Management Information System (GESMIS), launched December 2024 for staff and learner data — but these are not yet linked to a national data exchange. In September 2025, the National Identification Authority announced plans to integrate the student database with the Ghana Card, which would allow learners to use their national ID in place of separate school identification, but this integration had not been implemented as of the announcement and no operational cross-government exchange for education data yet exists.

revised_comments: Ghana operates the Ghana Labour Market Information System (GLMIS), a standalone portal run by the Labour Department for job seeker and employer registration. In early 2026 the Ministry of Labour, Jobs and Employment announced a new national digital platform intended to bring vacancies from government institutions, private employers and regulated overseas recruitment programmes into a single system, alongside newly established Public Employment Centres in all 16 regions; this platform was still under development and testing as of February 2026. There is no evidence that employment services data is integrated with a broader cross-government data exchange.

revised_comments: Ghana's judiciary has pursued digitisation through the Court Automation System and the e-Justice project (part of the World Bank-funded e-Transform programme, launched 2019), which provides electronic case filing, docket management and a Case Management System for the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal. However, a December 2025 IMF governance assessment found the e-Justice platform has stalled, citing unreliable connectivity, inadequate funding and continued reliance on manual processes in many courts. There is no evidence that court records or case management data are integrated with a wider government data exchange.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence of AI integration in Ghana's data exchange systems. NITA's DPI page describes data exchange hub as 'the missing link in Ghana's digitalization'. Ghana.gov and sector-specific portals (eTax, business registry) do not document AI/analytics capabilities for data exchange purposes.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) cited NITA's DPI page and the DIAL case study, both of which describe the exchange only as planned. Confirmed via the National AI Strategy 2025–2035 (launched April 2025) and the Data Harmonisation Bill 2025 consultation (Nov 2025) that the data exchange itself remains at proposal stage, so AI cannot yet be integrated into it. The Ghana Revenue Authority's standalone AI-powered customs fraud-detection tool (reported January 2026) sits within a single agency, not the cross-government exchange. Score changed from 0 to 1 (No) as this is a confirmed absence rather than a genuine unknown.
revised_comments: Ghana's National AI Strategy (2025–2035), launched April 2025, identifies the planned Data Exchange Hub as the future backbone for AI-enabled data quality, fraud detection and analytics across government, but this data exchange remains at the proposal stage: the enabling Data Harmonisation Bill 2025 only entered public consultation in November 2025. Separately, the Ghana Revenue Authority has deployed an AI-powered trade-data analytics tool for customs fraud detection, reported in January 2026 to have helped recover GH¢15 million, but this sits within a single agency rather than a cross-government data exchange. No AI or analytics capability is yet integrated into a national data exchange.
